title: Standardize metering for mixed cache + batch flows
creator: Elena Park
description:
Problem summary: Metering and quota accounting are inconsistent across requests that traverse multiple optimization layers: prefix/KV cache, prefetch, and request-level coalesced batching. We observe three classes of incorrect or unclear behavior in production and replayed traces: 1) partial cache hits where some tokens are served from KV cache and some are generated — tokens billed to origin model or zero-billed differently across routes; 2) coalesced batches (multiple logical requests aggregated into a single GPU invocation) where cost and quota attribution is currently split using a naive token-per-request share, which fails when requests have different priorities or were prefetched; 3) rate-limit enforcement applied before cache evaluation causes unnecessary rejections or double-charging during backfill and prefetch windows.

Goal: Define deterministic, auditable metering semantics for mixed-cache-batch flows and implement the enforcement + billing pipeline changes needed to make live billing, quota counters, and rate-limits consistent and explainable to customers and support staff.
technical_approach:
1) Spec a canonical token attribution model: every logical request receives an attribution tuple {billable_tokens, quota_consumed_tokens, origin}. billable_tokens = tokens actually produced by model runtime (excludes KV-prefix returns). quota_consumed_tokens = billable_tokens + prefetch_reservation if reservation semantics used. For prefetch/prefill we will introduce a lightweight reservation token that can be released if cache later answers fully.
2) Define batch-aggregation accounting: when coalescing requests, compute per-request billable_tokens after runtime returns per-request delta (we must propagate per-request KV cache hit masks through coalescer and runtime). The coalescer will emit an allocation vector used by billing.
3) Rate-limiting semantics: enforce soft reservation at ingress per-tenant/per-route using the same quota_consumed_tokens semantics, then apply hard enforcement after cache evaluation if reservation was not used. This avoids rejecting requests that are satisfied entirely by cache while still protecting the runtime.
4) Implement audit logs and deterministic event stream (billing-events) tied to request-id and tenant, with tags for cache_hit_mask, batch_id, prefetch_flag, kernel_variant.
5) Migrate metering pipeline in two phases: shadow-mode (produce billing-events but do not affect invoicing or quotas) for 2 weeks, then opt-in conversion for a subset of heavy customers before global roll-out.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical spec document published and reviewed by billing, infra, and legal
Billing-events contain per-request billable_tokens and quota_consumed_tokens for 100% of requests in shadow-mode traces
Shadow-mode runs for >=14 days with no unexplained delta >0.5% vs current invoices for a sampled tenant set
Rate-limiter preserves no-op behavior for cache-only hits (requests served entirely by cache do not decrement long-term quota) in opt-in run
End-to-end tests cover partial KV-hits, prefetch release, and coalesced batches with mixed priority requests
Dashboard shows cache-hit-adjusted cost and per-tenant monthly projection within 1% of model-runtime metering after opt-in conversion
tasks: Draft canonical metering semantics and review with Billing and Privacy teams
Implement cache-hit mask propagation in coalescer + runtime call path
Add reservation token API for prefetch flow and implement release logic
Produce billing-events from runtime including attribution vectors
Wire billing-events into existing invoice pipeline in shadow-mode (no charges)
Add E2E tests and augment integration test harness to simulate coalesced batches
Run shadow-mode for 14 days and collect deltas, iterate on edge cases
Perform canary opt-in for 3 enterprise tenants and validate invoices
Rollout change globally and update public billing docs
decisions: Use 'billable_tokens' (model runtime output tokens) as the canonical invoiced unit rather than request-level duration or GPU-seconds
Introduce a 'reservation token' for prefetch flows instead of immediately charging quota; reservations convert to consumption only if model produces tokens
Keep current per-token price model but add 'cache-savings' report line item for customers who wish to see separation
Batch coalescer must emit per-request delta; we will not retroactively split an opaque batch charge by proportional size at billing time because it is not auditable enough
tradeoffs: Reservation semantics add complexity to quotas (need to track outstanding reservations) but reduce billing disputes for cache-first flows
Emitting richer billing-events increases event volume and storage costs; however the auditability gain reduces customer support overhead and dispute churn
Delaying enforcement until after cache evaluation reduces false-rejects but requires a soft-reservation layer to protect capacity, adding engineering surface area

Need legal sign-off on reservation semantics for EU customers (privacy and invoicing rules)
notes: Implementation notes: when adding billing-events, ensure every event includes request_id, batch_id (if present), cache_hit_mask bitset as hex string, and a stable hashing of model variant to aid post-facto reconciliation. For long-running streams, emit checkpoint events once per 1k tokens so that downstream consumers can perform partial reconciliation without storing full traces. Support tooling: a small CLI utility (billing-replay) will allow reprocessing of events to simulate alternate metering rules for audits.
